name: Bao Quoc Pagoda
kicker: Sắc tứ temple on Ham Long hill
summary: An old hillside pagoda on Hàm Long hill, granted its royal charter and the name Báo Quốc in 1747. Climb through the triple gate into the court and the halls beyond. Give it 30 to 90 minutes for one of the Buddhist houses the Nguyễn lords honoured, an easy stop between the citadel and the tombs.
getThere: 17 Bảo Quốc street, Thuận Hóa ward, on Hàm Long hill.
heroCaption: The triple gate in the court at Bao Quoc

notice.title: Hours from one directory
notice.body: The gate hours, 07:00 to 17:00, come from the Hue pagoda directory only. Confirm them at the gate.

body: Báo Quốc stands on Hàm Long hill at 17 Bảo Quốc street, Thuận Hóa ward. Its old name is Hàm Long Thiên Thọ Tự, and the founder is Zen master Giác Phong, in the late 17th century. In 1747 Lord Nguyễn Phúc Khoát granted it the sắc tứ, a royal charter, and the name Báo Quốc.
Enter through the triple gate, then walk the court to the halls. The pagoda directory suggests a stay of 30 to 90 minutes and lists the gate as open from 07:00 to 17:00 every day.
